⑟. EU DECLARATION OF CONFORMITY

②. Article 74 information

Waste Battery Guidance for End Users

The following information is provided in compliance with Article 74(1)(a) to (f) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 on batteries and waste batteries.

aWaste prevention and battery lifecycle management

End-users play an important role in waste prevention. Good usage practices help extend the service life of this battery. Recommendations include avoiding deep discharge, preventing overcharging, and storing the battery in a cool, dry place at room temperature. At the end of its service life, this battery has potential options for re-use, preparation for re-use, preparation for repurposing, repurposing and remanufacturing.

bEnd-user obligation for separate collection

In accordance with Article 64 of the Batteries Regulation, end-users are obliged to send waste batteries into separate collection systems. This enables proper treatment and material recovery of battery components.

cCollection, take-back and treatment options for waste batteries

Waste batteries can be delivered to designated separate collection points and authorised take-back locations. Collected waste batteries will go through applicable processes including preparation for re-use, preparation for repurposing and professional waste treatment.

dSafety instructions for handling waste batteries

Waste lithium-ion batteries present risks such as short circuit, thermal runaway and fire hazard. Do not pierce, crush, disassemble, heat or short-circuit waste lithium batteries. Keep waste lithium batteries separated from combustible materials during storage and handling. In case of fire, use the extinguishing agents specified on this page.

eExplanation of battery markings and symbols

  • Crossed-out wheeled bin symbol: Batteries shall not be disposed of together with unsorted municipal waste and require separate collection.
  • Chasing arrows recycling symbol: It is a universal recycling mark to indicate the material is recyclable.
  • CE marking: Indicates conformity with applicable EU regulatory requirements.

fEnvironmental and health impacts of battery substances

Batteries contain substances, including hazardous substances. Improper disposal such as littering or discarding batteries into household residual waste may release hazardous substances into soil, water and air. These substances may harm ecosystems, the environment and human health. Proper separate collection and treatment help minimise these adverse impacts.
